subject.title: [Bug]: agents set-identity --workspace does not set the agent's stored workspace, but its success response implies it does

question: Should the public CLI solve existing-agent relocation by adding a dedicated workspace setter, by clarifying `set-identity` output only, or by repurposing `set-identity --workspace` as a setter?
rationale: Both the setter path and the JSON output shape are public CLI compatibility surfaces, so the source-proven mismatch needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Add Dedicated Setter
options.body: Add `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` backed by the existing Gateway update path, and make `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

options.title: Clarify Output Only
options.body: Keep relocation out of the CLI for now and add additive output/docs fields so `set-identity` cannot be read as confirming a stored workspace update.

options.title: Repurpose Set Identity
options.body: Make `set-identity --workspace` also update the stored workspace, accepting compatibility risk against the current locator help text and docs.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Setter
recommendation.body: Add `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` backed by the existing Gateway update path, and make `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is the public `agents set-identity` CLI contract originally introduced in this area.
